paper_title: Barbiturate end-capped non-fullerene acceptors for organic solar cells: tuning acceptor energetics to suppress geminate recombination losses

knowledge_points.content: The non-fullerene acceptors FTB and FTTB are synthesized via a two-step process: Suzuki coupling of 9,9-dioctylfluorene-2,7-diboronic acid pinacol ester with 2-bromo-5-formylthiophene, followed by Knoevenagel condensation with 1,3-dimethylbarbituric acid (for FTB) or 1,3-diethyl-2-thiobarbituric acid (for FTTB).
knowledge_points.evidence: Suzuki coupling of 9,9-dioctylfluorene-2,7-diboronic acid pinacol ester with 2-bromo-5-formylthiophene yields the aryl dialdehyde intermediate. Knoevenagel condensation of this intermediate with 1,3-dimethylbarbituric acid yields the final product FTB, whilst condensation with 1,3-diethyl-2-thiobarbituric acid yields FTTB.

knowledge_points.content: The substitution of a carbonyl group (C=O) with a thiocarbonyl group (C=S) in the barbiturate end-cap results in a deeper LUMO level and a red-shifted absorption spectrum due to the more polarizable nature of the thioketone group.
knowledge_points.evidence: FTTB has deeper HOMO (-5.8 eV) and LUMO (-3.7 eV) levels than FTB (-5.7 eV and -3.5 eV respectively), which can be attributed to the more polarizable nature of the C=S bond compared to C=O making the thioketone a stronger acceptor group... substitution is observed to have a more significant effect on the LUMO energy, resulting in a slightly reduced optical bandgap.

knowledge_points.content: Organic solar cells using the FTTB:PSEHTT blend achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 7.2% with a short-circuit current (JSC) of 13.5 mA/cm², while FTB:PSEHTT devices achieved a PCE of 5.4% and a JSC of 8.9 mA/cm².
knowledge_points.evidence: For PSEHTT:FTTB devices... yielded a PCE of up to 7.2%. Similar optimised conditions were found for PSEHTT:FTB leading to a PCE of up to 5.4%. The higher efficiency of the FTTB devices results from higher photocurrent generation (13.5 mA cm-2 compared to FTB 8.9 mA cm-2).

knowledge_points.content: The open-circuit voltage (VOC) of FTB-based devices (1.13 V) is significantly higher than that of FTTB-based devices (0.98 V), reflecting the higher LUMO level of the FTB acceptor.
knowledge_points.evidence: The higher efficiency of the FTTB devices results from higher photocurrent generation... offset in part by a lower open circuit voltage (0.98 V vs. 1.13 V). The higher VOC of the FTB devices is consistent with its higher LUMO level.

knowledge_points.content: FTTB:PSEHTT blends exhibit larger energy offsets (LUMO-LUMO offset of ~0.4 eV and HOMO-HOMO offset of 0.6 eV) compared to FTB:PSEHTT blends (LUMO-LUMO offset of ~0.2 eV and HOMO-HOMO offset of 0.5 eV).
knowledge_points.evidence: This stronger acceptor group creates larger LUMO-LUMO and HOMO-HOMO offsets between PSEHTT and FTTB (~0.4 eV and 0.6 eV respectively) compared to FTB in blends (~0.2 eV and 0.5 eV respectively).

knowledge_points.content: Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy (fs-TAS) reveals that the PSEHTT polaron absorption in the FTB blend undergoes a larger (40%) and faster (~650 ps) geminate decay compared to the FTTB blend (20% decay, 1.5 ns half-life).
knowledge_points.evidence: For the FTTB blend, a modest (20%) decay of polaron absorption... is observed with a decay half-life of 1.5 ns. By contrast, in the FTB blend, this decay is both larger in amplitude (40%) and faster (~650 ps).

knowledge_points.content: Optimized FTTB:PSEHTT devices were fabricated using a 1:2 blend ratio in a 10 g/L chlorobenzene (CB) solution without the use of thermal annealing or additives, as these treatments were found to reduce efficiency.
knowledge_points.evidence: For PSEHTT:FTTB devices, optimised conditions (1:2 blend ratio in 10 g L-1 CB solvent without annealing), yielded a PCE of up to 7.2%... We note that both processing additives and thermal annealing lowered the device efficiency.

knowledge_points.content: Space-charge limited current (SCLC) measurements indicate that both FTB and FTTB blends have similar charge transport properties, with electron mobilities around 3–6 × 10⁻⁵ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ and hole mobilities around 7–8 × 10⁻⁵ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹.
knowledge_points.evidence: Electron and hole mobilities for PSEHTT:FTB and PSEHTT:FTTB blends were both found to be similar. The electron mobility ranged from 3–6 × 10-5 cm2 V-1 s-1 while the hole mobility ranged from 7–8 × 10-5 cm2 V-1 s-1 for both systems.

knowledge_points.content: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) shows that FTB has a higher melting transition (230 °C) than FTTB (180 °C), which is attributed to the reduced steric bulk of the methyl groups in FTB compared to the ethyl groups in FTTB.
knowledge_points.evidence: FTB shows a higher melting transition with a peak at around 230 °C compared to FTTB (180 °C), consistent with the increased intermolecular interactions that are expected from FTB’s less bulky methyl groups.
